  "text": "By the following week, the bench had become a place people mentioned at the bakery. A man with a newspaper said the shade arrived three minutes late on cloudy days. Two sisters reported that the chestnut tree dropped its flowers into their hair. Neither sounded disappointed.

Imani went back one afternoon with a book, but found an older boy already sitting there. He was holding a closed notebook on his lap.

‘Is this the bench from the card?’ he asked.

She nodded and sat at the other end. For a while, they watched a beetle make its way along a crack in the pavement. The boy opened his notebook, wrote something, and shut it again.

When the shade reached Imani’s shoes, he stood up. ‘It works,’ he said.

At the bakery the next morning, Imani found a new card in the box. It said: If you have a question you cannot answer, write it down. Take it somewhere pleasant. You do not have to solve it there.

She read the card twice before showing it to her grandfather. He put it beside the photograph of the pastries, where everyone could see it.

That afternoon, Imani tore a corner from an old shopping list and wrote, Why do pigeons look surprised when they fly? She took the question to the bench and folded it into her pocket.

The shade reached her feet at four. She stayed until it reached her knees, then walked home without an answer. The question was still in her pocket, and she liked having it there."
